lines: overnight is a Claude Code plugin with a command that runs one piece of work in Claude Code while
you're away, and has it go on by itself after the usage limit or an error stops it.
overnight is for you when you hand Claude Code work that runs for hours, and leave it running at
night. With it, you find the work done by morning, or recorded as failed with its log, without
getting up to type "continue" once the limit lifts.
- overnight doesn't resume a conversation that you have open in Claude Code: it runs a work that
- overnight doesn't run from a terminal outside Claude Code: Claude Code puts the command on the
- overnight doesn't keep your computer awake: before you leave, set the computer not to sleep while
In development, at 0.1.0: overnight carries one work at a time. It doesn't yet keep a queue of
works, start the next work when one ends, or start a work at a given time.
overnight runs your work in Claude Code without you, and each time a run stops short, it waits and
asks Claude to go on in the same conversation, until the work is done or the retries run out.

more.good_when: A reader learns at the top, before they install, that no real night has yet carried a work through with this version, so they decide whether to trust a night's work to it knowing that; today they learn it only in the Walkthrough, after the install steps.
A reader who follows the MIT link reaches the license's full text; from the README's folder, the link leads to a file that isn't there.

A reader sees what a night with overnight gives them, and why they can trust it, before they're asked to set it up, so they install only once they've decided it fits; today Requirements and Installation come before the Walkthrough and How it works, and the note that no real night records the run comes after the install.

A reader sees a night that actually happened with this version: the command, the log of its stops and retries, and the done work in the morning; today the README says the run shown is the one overnight is built toward, and no night run of this version records it.

A reader with nothing set up runs the two install commands, then sees `overnight 0.1.0` from `! overnight --version`; today `claude plugin install overnight@ccpm` fails with `Plugin "overnight" not found in marketplace "ccpm"`.

A reader who follows the Changelog link reaches the list of changes in each version, and a reader who wants every option of the command, beyond the three the README shows, knows where to find them; today the Changelog link leads to a file that isn't there, and nothing points to the full set of options.
